flag_means: removes auto-merge eligibility; the bump goes to a gate
clear_means: no change; eligibility still comes only from the deterministic policy

breaking.instructions: Does `note` describe a change that can break an existing installation that upgrades without changing anything?

criteria.true: Upgrading as-is can fail or behave differently: removed support, removed or renamed settings, changed defaults that alter behavior, required manual steps.
criteria.false: Bug fixes, new optional features, documentation, deprecation warnings for a later release, or performance work.

needs_operator_step.instructions: Does `note` say an operator must run a step (a command, data migration, or manual change) as part of upgrading?

criteria.true: The note names an action to perform before, during, or after the upgrade, including changing a setting to a new name or value.
criteria.false: The upgrade needs no action from the operator.

removes_setting.instructions: Does `note` say a configuration value, setting, or flag has been removed in this release?

criteria.true: A setting no longer exists in this release, with or without a replacement.
criteria.false: No setting is removed in this release. A deprecation that announces a future removal is not a removal.

renames_setting.instructions: Does `note` say a configuration value, setting, or flag now has a different name?

criteria.true: The same setting moved to a new name or path.
